answer: No. JSON object member/key order is not semantically significant in the JSON data model. However, textual order can still be preserved or observed by particular parsers, data structures, or APIs as an implementation behavior or interface convention.
path: JSON data model semantics, distinguished from parser/API behavior
rationale: A JSON object is defined as an unordered collection of name/value pairs, so reordering members does not change its data-model meaning. Implementations may nevertheless retain insertion or source-text order and expose it to callers.
